subject.title: Design: run lifecycle reliability — bounded liveness, abort⇒release, crash resume, completion drive

question: Should maintainers adopt this issue as the canonical staged run-lifecycle reliability umbrella, and if so which Track A-D sequencing and compatibility tradeoffs are approved first?
rationale: The source evidence supports the problem class, but the proposed fix chooses cross-cutting lifecycle ownership, liveness thresholds, SQLite durability, Codex client retirement behavior, and terminal user-messaging policy across stable gateway surfaces.

options.title: Adopt Staged Umbrella
options.body: Approve the invariants as the maintainer-owned direction and review the existing Track A/B PRs plus later durability/completion PRs against those invariants.

options.title: Approve Only Track A First
options.body: Limit near-term approval to abort-to-release and stale takeover, leaving liveness thresholds, crash resume, and completion drive for later design decisions.

options.title: Keep Reports Separate
options.body: Decline the umbrella and continue landing narrow fixes against each existing production report without treating this issue as canonical.

recommendation.title: Adopt Staged Umbrella
recommendation.body: Approve the invariants as the maintainer-owned direction and review the existing Track A/B PRs plus later durability/completion PRs against those invariants.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored and self-assigned the umbrella and are already carrying the linked Track A/B implementation stack and follow-up design comments.
